races.name: Dine In Sherwoods Restaurant Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Cyrano De Bergerac
runners_data.note: Gosden-trained on a 12-day turnaround, proven on soft and standard going over 10f, and tags as a prominent runner who effectively leads here by default in a field of three; the STYLE_FIT flag is minor given he simply ends up in his natural position at the head of affairs, and his OR 120 with Luke Catton (3) claiming makes him the horse to beat if he transfers his placed form over a longer trip.

runners_data.name: Flag Of Eva
runners_data.note: Appleby's hold-up filly arrives on 24 days' rest with back-to-back sixth-place finishes including one over a similar trip on standard Southwell, but her single win came on similar going and Jack Dace (5) will need Cyrano to set a truly crawling pace for her late run to have any effect; the OR-level parity flatters a horse whose recent form has been well below the ceiling implied by that rating.

runners_data.name: Seacole
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's lightly-raced runner is the biggest unknown in the race — going UNKNOWN, style UNKNOWN, and no recent run date recorded — but Beckett's 14-day record of 8/58 reflects a yard in decent form and Pat Dobbs will have been briefed to get her into a good position tracking the leader; headgear noted (h), which could indicate a first-time hood or bit change designed to settle a potentially free-going or wayward filly.

races.paceDynamic: Cyrano De Bergerac is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this three-runner novice and will stride to the front unchallenged, dictating a controlled, sustainable tempo on Good ground over 1m2f at Nottingham. Flag Of Eva is a hold-up type who will sit last, while Seacole's style is unknown but her headgear and lightly-raced profile suggest she will slot in wherever connections dictate, likely tracking Cyrano in second. With no pressure on the leader and a small field, Cyrano sets an honest but uncontested gallop that will make this a test of stamina and finish rather than raw pace. This race shape strongly favours a horse with tactical versatility or a powerful staying finish — a genuine hold-up closer who can produce a sustained late run, or the front-runner if its class is high enough to exploit the soft tempo and kick clear before rivals can respond.

scenarios.body: If Cyrano De Bergerac settles comfortably in front and uses the uncontested lead to conserve energy before quickening in the straight.

scenarios.body: If the pace set by Cyrano De Bergerac is genuinely slow, allowing Flag Of Eva to close from last with a powerful sustained run in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.title: Unknown Seacole Lands

scenarios.body: If Seacole, the lightly-raced Ralph Beckett runner, has been produced significantly improved and tracks Cyrano before overwhelming the field with a superior turn of foot.

scenarios.body: If the slow uncontested pace compresses the field so all three finish within a length of each other and fine margins decide.

watchPoints.text: Watch Cyrano De Bergerac's early tempo — if Luke Catton (3) allows a crawl, the race becomes a sprint and his stamina advantage over 1m2f evaporates, opening the door for Flag Of Eva's late run.

Seacole's unknown going preference is a genuine concern on Good turf; if she has only been seen on an artificial surface or is highly inexperienced, Pat Dobbs may struggle to find her best position in a slowly-run three-runner race.

Flag Of Eva's form of 6-6 is uninspiring and both runs came over trips shorter than or at the same distance — monitor whether Appleby pitches her forward more aggressively than her hold-up tag suggests if the early pace is visibly slow.

With only three runners, any tactical error — such as Cyrano over-racing or Seacole missing the break — becomes magnified and could dramatically alter the finish order; small-field dynamics at Nottingham over 1m2f can produce messy, slowly-run affairs that reward the freshest or best-handicapped horse late.

races.name: Racedays For £9 At Nottingham Racecourse Training Series Apprentice Handicap (RE Series)

runners_data.name: Ramli
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner here, apprentice Kyle McHugh (3lb claim) takes the ride for Nick Littmoden who has had no runners in the last 14 days; Ramli's two wins have come at 8f and 10f, making this 1m½f a slight trip query, though its OR=82 gives it a class edge and good-going form reads as 2 from 4 with two places.

runners_data.name: Zowal
runners_data.note: John & Sean Quinn runner returning after 74 days off, which is a fitness question worth noting; a genuine hold-up type who has won on soft and good, but all five recent runs have been at 7f-8f, making this step to 1m½f an unproven distance stretch that tempers expectations despite OR=77 and Shay Farmer in the saddle.

runners_data.name: Lord Normandy
runners_data.note: Tom Clover's gelding is returning from a lengthy 232-day absence, which is the single biggest flag in this field; however, its form profile is notably distance-appropriate — a win at 10f on good ground and a placed effort at the same trip — and Molly Keegan-Price's 7lb claim could offset any burden, making it a live watch if match-fit.

runners_data.name: Leadenhall
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's six-year-old was out just seven days ago and the yard is in fine form at 8/104 over 14 days; a natural come-from-behind type whose wins have both come at 8f on good ground, it is racing in uncharted territory over 1m½f, and the style-fit tag reflects that it is unlikely to secure its preferred prominent position against this field shape.

runners_data.name: Equion
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's eight-year-old has been off 152 days and all recent runs have been over 8f on standard or AW surfaces — sim-going returns just 1 from 15 — making both the absence and the step up to 1m½f on turf significant concerns; apprentice Myla Coppins rides, and at OR=61 this is the bottom weight in the field.

races.paceDynamic: Ramli is the sole confirmed front-runner in a five-horse field and should lead from the gates over this 1m½f trip at Nottingham on good ground, setting a controlled, uncontested tempo that is unlikely to be pressured at any stage. With both Zowal and Lord Normandy carrying genuine hold-up profiles, the race will likely settle into a strung-out pattern early, with Ramli dictating fractions from the front and the hold-up horses forced to cover ground from off the pace in the straight. Leadenhall is a true hold-up type redistributed to midfield on the map because the field contains more come-from-behind horses than can all race at the rear simultaneously, but its natural style means it will likely race further back than shown. This race shape strongly favours horses who can sit prominently behind Ramli or track the leader into the straight, as the moderate single-file tempo will reward those in a position to strike without needing to make up significant ground late.

scenarios.title: Ramli Controls, Holds On

scenarios.body: If Ramli leads uncontested and the hold-up horses fail to close the gap in time.

scenarios.title: Closer Gets Up Late
scenarios.trigger: If Ramli sets an overly strong early pace and ties up in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Ramli sets an overly strong early pace and ties up in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Quickens Through
scenarios.trigger: If Leadenhall, despite redistribution, gets a better pitch than expected and delivers a prominent challenge.
scenarios.body: If Leadenhall, despite redistribution, gets a better pitch than expected and delivers a prominent challenge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Tactical Race
scenarios.trigger: If no horse settles cleanly into role and pace breaks down into a falsely run contest.
scenarios.body: If no horse settles cleanly into role and pace breaks down into a falsely run contest.

watchPoints.text: Lord Normandy has the most relevant distance profile in the field (wins and places over 10f on good), and if Tom Clover has this horse fit after 232 days off, it is the most dangerous threat to Ramli at the business end.

Ramli's entire win record is over 8f-10f — watch whether Kyle McHugh is instructed to settle it off the pace or whether it races prominently over the longer 1m½f trip, as any energy wastage early could cost it the race.

Leadenhall runs just seven days after its last outing and Tim Easterby's yard is in active form, but this horse has never been tried over 1m½f and its redistribution from a true hold-up style means it may struggle to get into the race from a natural position in a small five-runner field.

Zowal's 74-day absence combined with a clear step up in trip from its entire career profile (7f-8f) makes it worth monitoring in the market — any support would suggest connections are confident about both fitness and the distance test.

With only five runners on good ground at Nottingham, the draw and early positioning will be magnified — watch the early strides to see whether any of the hold-up horses (Zowal, Lord Normandy) attempt to track closer than expected, which would signal a change in tactical intent.

races.name: Wildwest Beer Festival 4th July Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Organ
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner in an uncontested lead scenario, proven in good-ground conditions with 11 runs in similar going, though at 44 days since last run and a 7lb claimer aboard, the key question is whether Harry Vigors can manage the pace accurately enough to preserve Organ's stamina through the final furlong; STYLE_FIT tag reflects that this horse is listed as Prominent but will effectively race as the lone leader.

runners_data.name: Model Yuko
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's four-year-old returns after a lengthy 289-day absence which is a significant fitness flag, but the single win on her record came in good-going conditions and Sean Bowen is an accomplished jockey in this discipline; if Varian has her primed, she profiles as the most natural challenger to Organ just off the pace, though the layoff must temper expectations markedly.

runners_data.name: Nolton Cross
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's seven-year-old holds a deep hold-up profile and races from the rear, but his record on good ground is poor — 0 wins and 0 places in 3 similar-going runs — and recent form figures of 9-8-13 suggest he is badly out of form; Luke Catton's 3lb claim does little to compensate for those concerns over this trip.

runners_data.name: Spoken Truth
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's five-year-old is the most interesting hold-up horse in the race, arriving fresh at 15 days since last run and boasting two second-place finishes in similar good-ground conditions; Callum Hutchinson is a less heralded pilot but the horse's course record of placing off honest gallops over 10f makes him a legitimate player if the pace stretches the field.

runners_data.name: Green Triangle
runners_data.note: Simon & Ed Crisford's four-year-old is a genuine hold-up type repositioned to midfield on the map because of the surplus of closers in this field — the STYLE_FIT flag is legitimate as its natural trailing position is unlikely to be available; headgear (tongue-tie/blinkers) and a record of 12 runs in good-going conditions with only one win are both contextual concerns, and recent form figures of 8-8-5-6 do not inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Time Loop
runners_data.note: William Haggas's five-year-old is a natural prominent racer — the redistribution to midfield reflects the congested pace positions, not his instinct to race up with the pace; he arrives with strong recent form including a win and two places on standard ground, but the bulk of that came on softer surfaces and his good-ground record is untested at this trip.

runners_data.name: Towerlands
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's four-year-old has a clear prominent style and a recent placed run over 10f on good ground in his last start, making him a solid pace-stalker who should track Organ without needing to overreach; 42 days since last run for a trainer in decent form at 11 wins from 51 in the last 14 days means freshness is not a concern, though a cluttered recent record including four non-winning runs needs to be weighed.

runners_data.name: Bella's Path
runners_data.note: Charlie Pike's four-year-old has been absent for 257 days — the longest layoff in the field — and while the horse's natural style is prominent, displacement to midfield on the map is unavoidable given the volume of pace; with only three career runs on record and a trainer operating at just 1 from 13 in the last 14 days, the unknown fitness factor here is the largest in the race.

races.paceDynamic: Organ is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will stride out unchallenged from the off over Nottingham's flat 1m2f trip, setting a controlled and sustainable gallop on good turf. Model Yuko and Towerlands are the most likely to press Organ into a genuine prominent position, but the field contains a surplus of prominent-minded horses — Time Loop and Bella's Path are natural prominent racers who will be forced to settle further back than they would prefer, with Green Triangle similarly displaced rearward despite being a genuine hold-up type. The resulting race shape is an orderly, single-file contest run at a steady-to-honest clip, with Organ able to dictate throughout and the closers likely covering ground on horses who are out of their natural rhythm. This race shape most favours horses who can race prominently and sustain their effort through the home straight — a clean front-runner or a horse travelling just off the pace in a genuine tracking role has a structural advantage, while true hold-up horses face a flat, unvarying gallop that offers no late injection of pace to play into their hands.

scenarios.title: Organ controls, holds on
scenarios.trigger: If Organ leads unchallenged and the pace remains controlled enough that no prominent rival has the energy to reel him in
scenarios.body: If Organ leads unchallenged and the pace remains controlled enough that no prominent rival has the energy to reel him in

scenarios.title: Prominent pair overhaul leader
scenarios.trigger: If Organ sets a pace that proves just quick enough to weaken him in the final furlong, leaving Model Yuko or Towerlands to collar him late
scenarios.body: If Organ sets a pace that proves just quick enough to weaken him in the final furlong, leaving Model Yuko or Towerlands to collar him late

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers finish strongest

watchPoints.text: Organ's pace control is the single biggest variable — if Harry Vigors (7lb claimer) misjudges the tempo and goes too slow, the field concertinas and Organ becomes a sitting target for Model Yuko and Towerlands in the straight.

Model Yuko's 289-day absence for Roger Varian needs live market confirmation — Varian's yard is known to return horses fit, but if the market drifts significantly at the off, her prominent challenge may be theoretical rather than real.

Time Loop and Bella's Path, both natural prominent types mapped to midfield, could cause an unsettled early race if either jockey attempts to push forward to their preferred position — watch the first two furlongs for any unexpected surge from Pat Dobbs or Kieren Fox.

Spoken Truth is the closest thing to a value hold-up profile in this race — David O'Meara's runner has placed twice on good ground at similar trips and arrives race-fit at 15 days since last run, making it the most credible alternative if Organ weakens late.

Green Triangle's headgear (tongue-tie and blinkers flagged) warrants noting — if the gear produces a sharper early reaction, the horse could push further forward than the map suggests, marginally tightening the field and affecting how cleanly Organ gets away.

races.name: It's Racing Staff Week Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Secret Mistral
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up performer placed in midfield on the map because the race has surplus closers; six years old, 176 days off, and a modest 1W4P record on similar going means confidence is limited despite the style fit being near-ideal on paper.

runners_data.name: Paradise Walk
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 6f Good and steps down to 5f, which may sharpen her up; a natural prominent racer, Jack Dace claiming 5lb, and her 1W1P record on Good ground makes her a credible tracker of Tiva if she settles into a forward position cleanly.

runners_data.name: Desert Treasure
runners_data.note: Two wins from two at 5f on Good ground and a strong 2W2P similar-going record mark her as the standout profile for this race shape; drop back from 0 in her last run is the only flag, but William Haggas with Pat Dobbs represents a top-shelf combination to restore form.

runners_data.name: Tiva
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner and the only horse who will dictate early terms; the visor is new headgear and she carries top weight, but her 3W7P record at 5f on Good and O'Meara's 7/55 14-day strike rate suggest she is well-placed to exploit her tactical advantage — note STYLE_FIT tag means she may race more prominently than ideally suited on a flat track with no pressure.

runners_data.name: Palmeira
runners_data.note: A true hold-up type mapped to midfield as the field is overstocked with closers; her five most recent runs are all finishes of 3rd-6th at 5f, and a 0W3P similar-going record and a short 7-day turnaround for Eve Johnson Houghton's yard (4/32 14-day) make her a hard horse to trust here.

runners_data.name: Elegant Erin
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old hold-up specialist whose 0W5P record on similar going is a blunt assessment of her recent ceiling; Tom Kiely-Marshall (5lb claim) is a positive, but she has finished in the bottom half of her field in four of her last five starts at 5f on Good.

runners_data.name: Sugar Hill Babe
runners_data.note: Won and placed at 5f on Good in her last two runs, making her the most live hold-up threat in the field; Lisa Williamson's yard is at 0/4 in the 14-day window which is a minor caution, but Sugar Hill Babe's 2W7P similar-going record highlights she finds the surface well.

races.paceDynamic: Tiva is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival disputing the lead, she will set a controlled, sustainable gallop from the off on good ground over this straight five furlongs at Nottingham. Desert Treasure and Paradise Walk will press from just off the pace in a prominent position, creating a modest early tempo that is unlikely to collapse the field but equally unlikely to produce a suicidal burn. This field contains more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Palmeira and Secret Mistral are genuine closers who will almost certainly be forced into a midfield berth rather than their preferred position off a strong pace. The controlled pace set by Tiva, with two prominent types tracking closely, shapes this race as a test of cruising speed and a short, sharp finish rather than a stamina-sapping grind — favouring horses who can travel prominently and quicken off a sound but unforced gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tiva Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Tiva dictates a smooth, uncontested lead and the pace stays honest without over-quickening, prominent trackers who travel smoothly into the straight will dominate.
scenarios.body: If Tiva dictates a smooth, uncontested lead and the pace stays honest without over-quickening, prominent trackers who travel smoothly into the straight will dominate.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Tiva crawls the early fractions and the field bunches, creating a sprint finish where hold-up horses get an unexpected closing run.
scenarios.body: If Tiva crawls the early fractions and the field bunches, creating a sprint finish where hold-up horses get an unexpected closing run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Tiva Outstays
scenarios.trigger: If Tiva's lead grows unchallenged to the point where she bowls along at a thoroughly leisurely clip and the field cannot coordinate a challenge.
scenarios.body: If Tiva's lead grows unchallenged to the point where she bowls along at a thoroughly leisurely clip and the field cannot coordinate a challenge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Blowout
scenarios.trigger: If an early incident or positional battle accelerates the early fractions and the race becomes a true stamina test for a 5f sprint.
scenarios.body: If an early incident or positional battle accelerates the early fractions and the race becomes a true stamina test for a 5f sprint.

watchPoints.text: Desert Treasure is the standout profile — two 5f Good wins and Pat Dobbs booked — watch whether she settles cleanly in a prominent position behind Tiva, as her chance depends entirely on travelling smoothly into the straight.

Tiva sets the tempo for the entire field; if she is slow away or fails to establish the lead cleanly, the race loses its shape and hold-up horses gain significantly more opportunity than the pace map assigns them.

Palmeira and Secret Mistral are genuine closers who will be tracking midfield rather than hunting off a strong pace — watch whether they are trapped wide or short of room in the straight, as either scenario removes what little hold-up opportunity exists.

Paradise Walk drops from 6f to 5f for the first time in her recent form; if she travels keenly in the early stages and fails to settle, she may burn out before the finish rather than delivering her best prominent-style run.

Sugar Hill Babe is the only hold-up horse in the field with a genuinely strong 5f Good record — if the pace is slow and the race compresses into a sprint finish, her 1/5f/GOO and 2/5f/GOO are the credentials to note.

races.name: Construction Day 14th October Handicap

runners_data.name: Ingleby Archie
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent runner for Adrian Nicholls who has placed at 6f on Good ground twice in recent starts; 10 days since last run is a positive freshness angle and Jack Garritty rides, with the horse's profile suiting a race where a lone front-runner sets a takeable tempo.|

runners_data.name: Cairdeas
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen takes over for Paul Midgley and this four-year-old holds a win and a second at 6f, but its true instinct is to race from the rear; squeezed forward by the volume of hold-up types in this field, it is likely to race in a position that does not perfectly suit its pattern.|

runners_data.name: Raffles Angel
runners_data.note: Genuine closer with a win at 6f on Good ground in its recent history — the strongest going-match in the field — and Ross Coakley partners; at 14 days fresh, the horse has claims if the race develops pace to close into, though the controlled tempo is a tactical obstacle.|

runners_data.name: Early Release
runners_data.note: David Evans has been in form (4/19 over 14 days) and this horse won last time out, but its recent form has come largely on Standard artificial surfaces; limited Good turf evidence (0W 1P from four runs) tempers confidence, and like Cairdeas it will be pushed closer to the pace than it prefers by the field composition.|

runners_data.name: Winchurch
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's consistent four-year-old arrives just nine days after its last run, carries top weight at 135lbs, and has won at both 5f and 6f on Good ground; Harry Vigors claims 7lbs and the horse's ability to settle midfield and quicken makes it the most versatile of the hold-up contingent in this race shape.|

runners_data.name: Holbache
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's eight-year-old veteran wears headgear, has won twice at 6f on Good ground in recent history and will lead from the front; Tom Kiely-Marshall takes the 5lb claim, and while 21 days since last run is standard, the horse's profile as a controlled pace-setter at a track and trip it handles well underpins its tactical importance even if rivals press close.|

races.paceDynamic: Holbache is the confirmed pace-setter here, a veteran front-runner with headgear who will stride to the front and attempt to control this 6f Nottingham contest on Good turf at a sustainable, measured tempo. With only one genuine leader in a six-runner field, the pace will be honest but not punishing — Holbache will not be harassed into overdoing it early. The hold-up contingent is deep: Cairdeas, Early Release, Raffles Angel and Winchurch all want to come from off the pace, but the field contains more hold-up types than the race shape can naturally absorb, meaning Cairdeas and Early Release — tagged as redistributed — are unlikely to settle as far back as their natural style demands. This race shape strongly favours horses who can track the leader in second or third and quicken through the final two furlongs, as a lone front-runner at a controlled pace on Good ground sets up ideally for a prompt, close-range challenge rather than a late, wide-sweeping surge from the back.

watchPoints.text: Winchurch is nine days fresh carrying top weight but has a 6f Good win and Appleby's in-form yard — if it travels prominently rather than deep into the hold-up pack, it is the most dangerous horse in the field to Holbache's lead.

Holbache's jockey Tom Kiely-Marshall (5lb claimer) sets the tactical tempo for the whole race — any misjudgement of the early fractions could either string the field out or allow a slow pace that invites a mass sprint finish.

Cairdeas and Early Release are genuine rear-runners forced into a midfield role by the weight of hold-up types in this field; watch whether they can settle cleanly at a position that is not natural, as traffic problems or overcrowding in the straight are a real risk.

Raffles Angel is the only runner in the field with a win on Good ground at this exact trip as its headline form; if the pace quickens sharply in the final two furlongs rather than grinding out, it becomes the most interesting late-challenge profile.

Trainer T14 strike rates are notably strong for David Evans (4/19) and Michael Appleby (3/23), suggesting both Early Release and Winchurch arrive with their stables in a productive vein — neither should be casually dismissed despite the difficult hold-up dynamic.

races.name: Nottingham Racecourse Supporting Racing Staff Week Handicap

runners_data.name: Kalokalo
runners_data.note: Won over course and distance at Nottingham most recently and brings clear front-running credentials; Harry Vigors claims 7lb and Charles Hills is 1-from-10 over 14 days, so trainer form is modest, but the positional advantage on a track where leaders are rarely given up easily makes this the race to beat — note the STYLE_FIT tag reflects its prominent rather than lead label, a marginal distinction here.

runners_data.name: Distorted Truth
runners_data.note: Pat Dobbs rides for K R Burke who has been busy (9/53 in 14 days) but without a strong strike rate; 43 days off the track is the longest absence in the field and the horse's sole win came at 11f on Standard, making this 1m2f Good trip slightly unproven — a true hold-up type whose best chance arrives only if the pace surprises on the high side.

runners_data.name: Miss Pretty
runners_data.note: Georgia Dobie takes the ride for Edward Smyth-Osbourne whose yard is 0-from-7 in the past fortnight, a muted trainer stat; her sole win came over 7f on Standard suggesting she has pace, and a prominent style means she could slot in behind Kalokalo and turn this into a two-horse race in the straight — the step up to 1m2f is the key unknown.

runners_data.name: Mr Bollinger
runners_data.note: Fitted with headgear (p — presumably a hood or similar) which is worth noting as a first-time or reapplied equipment angle; Michael Bell has a modest 3-from-26 recent record and the horse has finished no better than fourth in three starts, all on either Soft or Standard surfaces — a true hold-up horse that needs a genuinely run race on Good ground it hasn't yet encountered.

runners_data.name: Astracornus
runners_data.note: David Menuisier has a reasonable 3-from-17 strike rate recently but this horse is 0-from-3 and all form has come on Good or Standard at 10f, so the trip is consistent — mapped to midfield due to redistribution of hold-up types, it is a natural rear-of-field runner and its chance hinges on race conditions that favour closers, which this pace map does not currently anticipate.

races.paceDynamic: Kalokalo is the lone confirmed front-runner in a field of five and, with no genuine pressure expected, should be allowed to dictate a sustainable gallop from the off over this 1m2f trip on Good turf. Miss Pretty is the only other horse with a prominent style and may attempt to track Kalokalo closely, but the pace is unlikely to be injected with any urgency given the absence of a rival to push the leader. Distorted Truth, Mr Bollinger, and Astracornus are all hold-up types by nature, meaning the field will be strung out early with the race shape heavily front-loaded and the rear contingent dependent on a meaningful tempo that may never materialise. This race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently or track the leader in a position to strike, as a controlled pace over 1m2f on Good ground typically sets up a finish for those closest to the pace rather than those waiting from deep.

watchPoints.text: Kalokalo is the lone confirmed pace-setter and any interference at the start or early bump from Miss Pretty challenging for the prominent position would significantly disrupt the expected race shape.

Miss Pretty's jockey Georgia Dobie is a conditional/amateur type taking on a small field — watch whether she opts to sit close to Kalokalo or drops in behind, as that tactical decision will define whether this becomes a genuine two-horse race from the front.

Mr Bollinger's headgear is flagged — confirm whether this is a first-time application, as debut headgear in a small field on Good ground can trigger unpredictable early speed and briefly alter the early pace.

With three hold-up horses (Distorted Truth, Mr Bollinger, Astracornus) all needing to close from behind in a five-runner race at a controlled tempo, watch for a bunched finish if Kalokalo's stamina gives way late — the winner may come from further back than the pace map suggests only in that scenario.

The going has been confirmed Good across all six races at Nottingham today with no deterioration — conditions are consistent and unlikely to produce unexpected surface quirks that would benefit any specific profile.
